_comment: PRD 10.6: absences are weighted, and the weight is data. This file is that data.
Nothing here is settled — PRD 14.13 says the numbers are unknown. These are
starting figures, in one place, changeable without touching engine code.
Tier shares come out roughly 2/3 : 1/3 : rounding error, per decision 102.
_threshold: 78 -> 25, read off a real result on 6 Aug 2026 per decisions 101 and 114.
78 was tuned against the 24 FICTIONAL seed creators, who were written to
demonstrate the model and therefore scored like the model's best case. Run
against 20 real creators the distribution is 0-34, median 19. A bar of 25
lets 5 through (25%), which is the read of 'about a quarter clear it'.
READ THE SECOND PARAGRAPH OF _effortSupport BEFORE TRUSTING THIS NUMBER.
A first attempt read the bar at 27 off a run where every classify call was
400ing silently. This figure is from the re-run with the classifiers live,
which moved several scores by 5-7 points in BOTH directions — propose_places
started working, more places got checked, and creators who looked like they
were missing things turned out to have them. A measurement is only worth
the error rows you checked before reading it.
READ THIS BEFORE REUSING THE NUMBER. 25 is not a general threshold — it is
the threshold for a cohort whose DEMAND IS STRUCTURALLY ZERO. All 20 scored
0 of 25 on Demand, with a signal count of 0, on the run where the classifier
was verified working — so this is the honest 'no readable comments' result
and not the silent failure above. 14 of the 20 have no YouTube channel, and
YouTube is the only place comments can legitimately be read (decision 110).
The ceiling for this cohort is Missing 35 + Pressure 34 = 69, so 78 was not
merely high, it was UNREACHABLE.
The consequence: a future cohort with readable comments carries up to 25
points this one cannot, and 25 would wave through creators this measurement
never looked at. Re-read the bar the first time a cohort has real Demand.
It is an admin setting precisely so nobody has to be right on day one.
houseBrief: Anyone worth a call — they make something clippable, in a format they can repeat, in a category people actually want.
_houseBrief: Q20: Fit is a gate and a gate has two values. `unknown` existed only because the
CLI let you leave --brief out. Scout PRD 6.1 says the house brief always exists, so
this is the floor rather than a default — the engine refuses to score without one.
Change the words here, not in the code.
6 Aug 2026 — THE WORDS AFTER THE DASH ARE LEAD, NOT DECORATION. PRD 6.1 names the
house brief 'Anyone worth a call' and describes it as 'big audience, no business,
under pressure'. That description is what the SCORE measures — Missing is 35 points
of no business, Pressure is 40 points of under pressure. Run against real people on
6 Aug it was handed to the Fit judge as the brief, and Fit stopped being a gate and
became a second, eyeballed copy of the score: creators were failed for 'only 12k
followers' and 'no sign of pressure', which are the exact facts the score had
already counted. The two highest scorers on the board, 34 and 32, both failed.
PRD 194 says what belongs here instead: the old global Format Fit — clippability, a
repeatable format, category demand. Distinctiveness is deliberately NOT in the list;
PRD 269 moved it to Trajectory, and putting it back would be the same bug again.
A gate must test something the score does not, or it is not a gate.

_comment: Task 4, 6 Aug 2026 — a brief, a handful of candidates, a drop.
DEMO-SCOPED, AND THE NUMBERS SAY SO. Q24 defers discovery at scale and that
still holds: maxCandidates is 20 because one model call over one brief is the
whole of the finding step here. This is not a crawler and nothing downstream
should read it as one.
creatorConcurrency parallelises across PEOPLE. It is safe to raise because the
per-host politeness delay is reserved synchronously in lib/http.js, so twenty
creators all wanting substack.com still arrive perHostDelayMs apart. Raising it
makes the drop finish sooner without making anyone's server busier — the host
queue, not this number, is the binding constraint, and `warhol drop` prints how
much of the wall clock went to waiting on it.
dropCap is Scout PRD 5.4's cap of about ten: the cap protects attention, the
threshold protects trust. Some days three names, some days zero.

retention._comment: Q18 / Scout PRD 12.1: keep the decisions, drop the evidence. Evidence for a creator who never surfaced in a drop ages out after this many days; conclusions never do. Run: warhol forget --confirm.

demandAlignment._comment: Decision 102: an absence counts more when the demand points straight at it. An item with every demand signal aimed at it is worth 1.75x its base weight.

demandCurve._comment: Saturating: points = demandMax * n / (n + halfPoint). 1,940 signals ~= 87% of the maximum; 200 ~= 40%; 50 ~= 14%.

_comment: Q6, 6 Aug 2026: cadence_decay flipped to needsHistory:false, because with the
YouTube Data API it genuinely computes on a FIRST look. YouTube stamps every
upload with its publish date, so the change over time is already in the data —
one visit reads it. Nobody stamps a follower count, which is why
unanswered_audience stays true and Trajectory still needs two looks.
So one of these four is unavailable on day one, not two, and the day-one
Pressure ceiling is 34 of 40 rather than 22. The ceiling printed on a report is
per creator, not this figure: a creator with no readable YouTube has no posting
history either, and their report says 22 and why.
declineFloor/declineFull scale the cadence points: no points until the posting
rate is down declineFloor, full max at declineFull. A quarter off is inside
ordinary variance for a person who makes things; four fifths off is a different
sentence about their life.
Q6: the sampling window for posting cadence, and how much of the comment
section to read. These are quota decisions as much as accuracy ones — a list
call costs 1 unit whatever maxResults says, so the bill is PAGES, not videos.
A full sweep is at most 1 + maxPages + maxPages = 9 units against a free tier
of 10,000/day, and Study adds one per video whose comments we read.
maxPages caps the upload walk at 200 videos. A creator who posts more often
than that in a year does not get a cadence reading — the sample cannot reach
back far enough behind the recent window to compare against, and the report
says exactly that rather than comparing against a window it never saw.
_budget: A YouTube comment can be 10,000 characters, and 500 of them would be a 5MB
prompt on a paid call. Purchase intent is short — 'where do I buy this' is 20
characters — so a comment is cut at maxCommentChars and the whole demand input
at maxDemandChars, comments first because they are the better signal. Both
trims are logged: a cap nobody can see reads as 'we looked at everything'.
_maxDemandChars: Lowered 60000 -> 20000 on 6 Aug 2026. 60k was sized for a creator with a busy
YouTube comment section; measured against the real cohort, 14 of 20 have no
readable comment section at all and the rest are thin, so the cap was paying
for headroom nobody used. Purchase intent is short and comments are sorted
best-first, so the signal is at the top of the input and the tail is where
the money went. Raise it again the day a cohort actually hits the cap — the
trim is logged, so that day is visible rather than guessed at.

_comment: 6 Aug 2026 — the second demand source, and the reason the first one was not
enough. Measured across the real cohort, 14 of 20 creators had no readable
comment section anywhere and Demand read a flat zero for all of them, which
capped the whole board at 34 of 100. Reddit is where people talk about a
creator when the creator is not in the room — unmoderated by the person being
discussed, which makes it a better demand source than a comment section.
Needs REDDIT_CLIENT_ID and REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET (a free 'script' app at
reddit.com/prefs/apps). The keyless JSON endpoints are gone — verified 6 Aug,
www.reddit.com/.json, old.reddit.com and api.reddit.com all answer 403 to any
client. Without the credential this source reports itself unavailable and the
report says we could not read, never that there was nothing to read.
minHandleChars IS THE SAFETY RULE, not a tuning knob. A short handle matches
other people's conversations, and attributing a stranger's demand to this
creator would put a fabricated quote on a report through a door that neither
keepOnlyRealQuotes nor the wall watches. 6 characters is the point below which
a word-boundary match stops being evidence. An unread creator scores neutral;
a misread one scores somebody else's audience, so refusing is the cheap error.
12 Aug 2026 — the first new enumerable source since YouTube, and the only
one on the shortlist that needs no key, no credential and no quota.
public.api.bsky.app/robots.txt grants crawling in writing and uses 429 as
its backoff signal, so this goes through lib/http.js like every other read
rather than around it like youtube.js and reddit.js.
maxFeedPages IS THE CADENCE LEVER. RSS ships 10-15 items and cannot reach
back the ~150 days the baseline arithmetic needs, which is why feed cadence
only computes for monthly publishers. getAuthorFeed is paginated, so this
cap is a BACKSTOP, not the plan: the walk stops as soon as it holds a post
older than youtube.baselineWindowDays, because the arithmetic clamps its
baseline to the oldest post in hand and every page after that cannot change
the answer. Measured live 12 Aug 2026, that is 2 pages for a creator who
posts weekly and 20 for 404 Media, rather than 20 for both.
20 x 100 is what it takes for the busiest accounts to reach back past the
90-day window plus its 60-day baseline: 404 Media posts ~157 a month, and at
6 x 50 their 300 posts only reached back 30 days -- cadence came back
unreadable for exactly the prolific creators this feature exists to read.
When the cursor runs out first we hold every post the account has, and
lib/bluesky.js passes truncated:false so the report may say 'their whole
account is N days old'. Otherwise it passes truncated:true.
maxBodyBytes is raised over the 600KB default because a page of 50 posts
with embeds runs past it, and a truncated body is a JSON syntax error --
which reads as a broken endpoint rather than as a read we cut short.
replyPosts/maxReplies bound the demand read. These are REPLIES UNDER THEIR
OWN POSTS, which is a comment section: searchPosts answers 403 without a
session, so there is no keyless route to what strangers say when the
creator is not in the room. Reddit is still the only source for that.
minHandleChars guards the CONSTRUCTED domain handles, {handle}.com and
.co. Those are earned rather than guessed because Bluesky binds a domain
handle with a DNS TXT record at _atproto.<domain> that only the domain's
controller can set -- so a domain handle that resolves proves control.
What it does not prove is that the domain is THIS creator's, and for a
short or ordinary handle it very often is not: 'cnn' would hand us a large
company's account and print its followers as this creator's.
5, NOT reddit.js's 6, AND MKBHD IS WHY. At 6 the floor excluded 'mkbhd' --
five characters, and mkbhd.com is the case this whole path was built for.
The two numbers guard different things: reddit.js is refusing a word that
matches other people's prose, and length is a good proxy for that. Here the
question is whether a domain belongs to somebody else, where length is only
a crude stand-in for how ordinary the word is. 4 and under is where the
handles stop being names and start being initials -- cnn, espn, hbo.

trajectoryGate._comment: Decision 104: test the audience, never the posting rate. Fail only when down over 12 months AND still falling over 3. Needs two observations at least 90 days apart, so a first look returns not_established — which is not a pass and not a fail.

youtubeGap._comment: PRD 5.2: no YouTube against a LARGE short-form audience is the highest-value line. Below this floor the absence is not worth the top weight, so it is demoted to tier 2 weighting.

_models: Two jobs, two models, split 6 Aug 2026. The split already existed as an
EFFORT setting; this makes it a model setting too, for the same reason.
CLASSIFY is extraction. 'Pull the comments that ask where to buy' and 'pull
the lines where they say they cannot keep up' are find-the-string tasks, and
keepOnlyRealQuotes throws away anything the model did not copy verbatim from
the text we supplied — so a weaker model cannot smuggle in a fabrication, it
can only miss one. The failure mode is a missed signal, which scores neutral
and lowers confidence, which is the behaviour PRD 11.3 already specifies for
a signal we could not read.
JUDGE is a judgment and stays on the strongest model. judgeFit decides
whether a person matches a brief, and Fit is a GATE (5.4) — a wrong verdict
here does not lower confidence, it silently admits or excludes someone. Same
for proposeCandidates, which is 11.1's one genuinely model-shaped job.
Measured reason for the split: the real cohort is 20 creators x 3 calls, and
on Opus that is roughly $1-3.50 a run when a run has to happen several times
before the threshold is read. On this split it is well under a dollar.
Do NOT collapse these back to one model to simplify the config. The line
between them is the same line the wall is drawn on (store.js): a model may
propose and it may extract, but the things it is trusted to DECIDE are few
and they are worth paying for.
_effortSupport: Not every model takes the effort parameter, and sending it to one that
does not is a 400 — not a degraded call, a REJECTED one. Found 6 Aug 2026
the expensive way: the classify job had just moved to Haiku 4.5, every
classify_demand, classify_strain and propose_places call 400'd with 'This
model does not support the effort parameter', and the run still completed
and still printed scores. Demand read 0 across all 20 creators and looked
exactly like the honest 'no readable comments' result it was supposed to
be. A threshold was read off that run before anyone noticed.
The lesson is not about this parameter. A model call that fails silently
and scores neutral is indistinguishable from a model call that ran and
found nothing — and §11.3 makes 'found nothing' a legitimate outcome, so
the failure wears the costume of a designed behaviour. Anything added
here must be checked against the error rows in costs.jsonl, not against
